messages:
cami (sec-eng): heads-up — our staging perf-test backups are failing decrypts during automated restores. started seeing AccessDenied in the KMS audit logs around 02:14 UTC. suspect recent RBAC cleanup removed a grant for the backup-uploader service account.

noah (eng-ops): saw the same alert. ot-bot posted: 
```
OT-BOT: KMS API Call: Decrypt FAILED
key: arn:aws:kms:us-east-1:111222333:key/abcd-ef01
principal: svc-account/backup-uploader-staging
error: AccessDeniedException
request_id: r-0a1b2c3d
```

lisa (db-ops): interesting — we did a role rename last week (backup-uploader -> svc-backup-uploader) as part of the IAM cleanup. did we also migrate grants? iirc grants are keyed to the principal ARN.

mike (sre): yep that explains it. RBAC rename + grant TTL + no rotation script = deleted effective access. quick question: do we prefer ephemeral grants (create-on-restore) or persistent grants attached to the key with IAM principals?

cami (sec-eng): for customer-facing restores we want as little manual intervention as possible. ephemeral grants are better security-wise, but we need automation to create them when the restore starts. also audit logging needs to show the grant lifecycle for compliance.

noah (eng-ops): as a stopgap i pushed a policy that allows the staging uploader role to call kms:Decrypt via a conditioned policy. PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/489 — please review.

lisa (db-ops): can we add a small canary job that actually attempts a decrypt against the latest snapshot key after every role change / IAM deploy? idea: schedule a k8s CronJob that runs `aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://snapshot-header.enc` and fails if AccessDenied.

mike (sre): agree. also add an alert that correlates KMS AccessDenied events with a recent IAM role change (CloudTrail event -> create/update role/policy). we had a blind spot: we logged AccessDenied but didn't link it to IAM config changes.

ot-bot (audit-bot): FYI — current audit retention has the relevant CloudTrail events, but we don't surface an automated signal that maps key-grant deltas to failing decrypts. filing ticket INFRA-1123 to track.

cami (sec-eng): action items: 1) merge noah's temp policy and rollback once we have an automated grant-on-restore flow (owner: noah). 2) create a canary decrypt CronJob in staging (owner: lisa). 3) add an alert that correlates CloudTrail IAM changes + KMS AccessDenied (owner: mike). 4) update encryption runbook with steps to recreate grants and add the audit proof checklist for compliance reviews (owner: cami).

noah (eng-ops): question for runbook — what TTL should ephemeral grants use if we go that route? default suggestion: 12h for restore window, but shorter (1h) for automated short-lived pipelines.

lisa (db-ops): 12h sounds fine for human-triggered restores. add logic: if restore is automated as part of CI (non-prod), use 30m TTL and require audit tag `ci=true`.

mike (sre): note on implementation — KMS grants can't be created cross-account with the same semantics; if we need cross-account restores we'll need grant proxies or a re-encryption step into a key in the target account. document that in the runbook.

cami (sec-eng): good call. also capture evidence requirements: for each restore we need CloudTrail entries for CreateGrant/DeleteGrant and the Decrypt call with the request id saved in the restore ticket. auditors will want that chain.

noah (eng-ops): I'll add a small metadata file to restore artifacts containing `kms_key_arn`, `grant_id`, `decrypt_request_id` for traceability.

lisa (db-ops): quick config snippet for the canary CronJob I'm going to land: 
```yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: CronJob
metadata:
  name: kms-decrypt-canary
spec:
  schedule: "@hourly"
  jobTemplate:
    spec:
      template:
        spec:
          containers:
          - name: canary
            image: amazon/aws-cli
            command: ["/bin/sh","-c","aws kms decrypt --ciphertext-blob fileb://canary.enc --output json"]
          restartPolicy: OnFailure
```

mike (sre): perfect. please make the job emit a metric on success/failure to CloudWatch/Prometheus. we'll alert on >3 failures in a row.

cami (sec-eng): thanks everyone. once PRs land, assign owners and I'll update the encryption playbook and run the compliance evidence checklist for last week's role rename so we can close the audit gap. :thumbsup:

noah (eng-ops): on it, will follow up in INFRA-1123.

ot-bot (audit-bot): Ticket INFRA-1123 created: "Canary + alerting for KMS decrypt failures correlated to IAM changes".
